prompt.context: Your client is a regional commercial bank. You have been asked to make a recommendation to improve the profitability of the retail segment of their business operations.
prompt.question: The CFO has proposed a commission-based incentive program targeted at the bank's tellers with the objective of increasing product sales. How much commission should the bank pay its tellers per unit of product sold?

clarifying_info.q: What products are included in the commission program?
clarifying_info.a: The bank has four products: CDs, Checking accounts, Mutual Funds, and IRAs.

clarifying_info.q: What are the profit margins and average deposit sizes for each product?
clarifying_info.a: CDs: 2% margin, $4,000 average initial deposit. Checking: 4% margin, $2,000 average initial deposit. Mutual Funds: 1% margin, $8,000 average initial deposit. IRAs: 2% margin, $4,000 average initial deposit.

clarifying_info.q: What are the tellers' current salaries?
clarifying_info.a: Average salary per year per teller: $25,000.

clarifying_info.q: How many products does each teller sell?
clarifying_info.a: Expected sales per teller: 5 products per week.

framework: Understand the product mix and profitability of each product
Calculate the profit per product (profit margin x average deposit) to determine the commission ceiling
Explore different incentive program structures (fixed fee, percentage of profits, tiered/threshold-based, variable by product)
Select the best incentive structure based on profitability impact, administrative cost, and employee motivation
Quantify the cost of the incentive program relative to teller salaries and sales volume
Deliver a specific commission figure and assess implementation implications

questions.prompt: Calculate the profit per product for each of the four products. What is a reasonable single average profit figure to use as the commission ceiling?
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply each product's profit margin by its average initial deposit. All four products yield $80 profit each: CDs = 2% x $4,000 = $80; Checking = 4% x $2,000 = $80; Mutual Funds = 1% x $8,000 = $80; IRAs = 2% x $4,000 = $80. The uniform $80 profit per product simplifies commission design.

math.setup: Profit per product = margin% x average initial deposit. Calculated for each product.
steps: All products yield $80 profit per unit — use $80 as the commission ceiling.
math.answer: $80 profit per product across all four products

questions.prompt: What incentive program structures could the bank use? Explore at least four options.
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm at least four structures: (1) Fixed fee per product sold; (2) Percentage of profits per product; (3) Fixed fee with a declining rate above a threshold (tiered); (4) Variable commission depending on product type and spread. A strong candidate may suggest additional creative options.

questions.prompt: Given that all tellers are equally effective sellers and all products require roughly the same effort to sell, which incentive structure would you recommend and why?
questions.guidance: The fixed fee option is best: it is a straightforward incentive with large upside for employees, and administrative costs are lower than variable or tiered structures. Candidate should justify choice based on simplicity, motivation, and cost-to-administer.

questions.prompt: Calculate an appropriate fixed commission fee. How does the commission affect the bank's profit margin per product?
questions.guidance: Candidate should anchor commission to teller salary and expected sales volume to ensure the cost is meaningful but not excessive. Annual sales per teller = 5 products/week x 50 weeks = 250 products/year. A $10 fixed commission is reasonable. New profit margin = $80 - $10 = $70 per product.

math.setup: Annual sales per teller = products per week x weeks per year. Commission should be reasonable relative to salary and profit per product.
steps: Annual sales per teller = 5 x 50 = 250 products per year
Annual commission cost per teller = 250 x $10 = $2,500
Annual commission as % of salary = $2,500 / $25,000 = 10% — meaningful incentive
math.answer: Recommended commission: $10 per product. New profit margin: $70 per product.

brainstorming.prompt: What criteria would you use to evaluate and compare the incentive program options?

categories.name: Profitability
ideas: Ease of sale for each product
Whether all tellers are equally effective sellers
Profit per teller or per customer
Estimated commission as a percentage of current salary
Total cost of the incentive program

categories.name: Human Capital
ideas: Which program best motivates employees to sell products
Fairness and transparency of the commission structure

recommendation: Implement a fixed fee commission of $10 per product sold across all four product lines (CDs, Checking, Mutual Funds, IRAs).
This yields a new profit margin of $70 per product and provides tellers a meaningful 10% salary uplift if they hit expected sales targets (250 products/year).
risks: Tellers may push products that are easiest to sell rather than products that best fit customers, creating compliance or suitability risk.
If tellers are not equally effective, high-performing tellers will benefit disproportionately, which may demotivate lower performers.
Commission cost assumptions depend on the 5-products/week estimate; if actual sales are higher the program cost could exceed projections.
next_steps: Add a tracking field in the accounting system to associate each sale with the correct teller ID for accurate commission attribution.
Update payroll systems to accommodate the new variable commission component.
Launch a sales training program for tellers to ensure product knowledge and appropriate selling practices.
Conduct an effectiveness study after 6-12 months to measure impact on employee retention, satisfaction, and revenue per teller.
